newsitem.title: USA: Restart of Citgo's Texas aromatic units on track.
newsitem.headline: Restart of Citgo's Texas aromatic units on track.

text.p: The restart of units downed but not damaged by an alkylation unit fire earlier this week at Citgo's Corpus Christi, Texas, refinery is on track, a Citgo official said Thursday morning.

"All of these units, except the one (alkylation unit) are in various stages of being returned to service," said Citgo spokesman Barbara Moore, reading from a prepared statement released late Wednesday.
She said damage assessment by Citgo teams on the fire-damaged 20,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) alkylation unit will continue for the next several days.
"It will be several days before the complete assessment of damage is completed," Moore said.

Citgo officials declined to estimate either when the unit, which produces high quality gasoline blending components, will be returned to service, or how much the damage will amount in financial terms.
In response to a question, Citgo's head spokesman Kent Young told Reuters on Wednesday the company is insured for such damage.

Among the affected units Citgo is restoring or has restored to service are aromatic plants that make cumene, benzene/tolulene/xylene (btx), a "hydrar" that hydrogenates cyclohexene, a petchem feedstock, and a "udex" unit.
Citgo Petroleum Corp is the U.S. unit of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela SA.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk, 1 212 859 1620
